solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rabbits who enlivened TV programme?

parts.note: in British slang to rabbit is to talk at length, so rabbits means chats

indicators.note: enlivened suggests the letters of the word who are stirred up and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A question about which rabbits brought some life to a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to rabbit is to chatter; 'who' is the anagram fodder for 'enlivened', not a pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast in which a host and guests talk informally is a type of television programme.

clue.text: Alternative therapist in love course

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a path is a course

explanation.surface: A complementary therapist taking a course on love.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeopathy is a form of alternative medicine and its practitioner is such a therapist.

clue.text: Had understood

definitions.meaning: to be had is to be deceived, fooled
to take something in is to understand it

explanation.surface: Had understood.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both deceived by a trick and grasped mentally.

clue.text: Area in public building conforming to Islamic law

indicators.note: in puts the area letter inside the public building

parts.note: a hall is a public building

explanation.surface: A section of a civic building set aside for Muslim religious practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside HALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or practice permitted under Islamic religious rules is described with this Arabic word.

clue.text: Women's best classes used to be

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
A grades are the top classes, so the plural is As

explanation.surface: Women's top classes are a thing of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb to be means existed, or used to be.

clue.text: Win over millions after westward attack across sierra

indicators.note: after places the millions abbreviation behind the rest of the wordplay
across means the reversed attack is laid over, around, the sierra letter
in an across clue westward means read from right to left, backwards

parts.note: a raid is an attack
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A battle report: a victory won with a westward attack across mountain ranges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westward' turns RAID into DIAR; 'across' puts it around S to give DISAR, and M comes 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone over is to charm away their hostility, which is the figurative sense of removing their weapons.

clue.text: Tree-trimmer perhaps the type to make Christmas speech?

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec
an orator is the type of person who makes a speech

explanation.surface: Someone decking the Christmas tree is the sort to give a festive address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the type to make ... speech' gives ORATOR, with DEC from 'Christmas' placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adorns a Christmas tree with tinsel and baubles is one example of a person who decks things out.

clue.text: Scrap box for article in sale

indicators.note: for means the box word stands in place of the article within the sale word

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
to box is to hit, to cuff

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out over a box of goods at a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the A in SALE for CUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a brief, confused fight, also called a tussle.

clue.text: Early magistrate turning up the day before queen

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: an eve is the day before a festival
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An old-time magistrate arriving the day before the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses EVE + ER, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval English official who kept the peace in a town or district was an early local magistrate.

clue.text: Siberian city's written matter, with adequate binding

indicators.note: binding means the adequate letters wrap round the written matter

parts.note: OK means adequate, satisfactory
MS is a manuscript, written matter

explanation.surface: A city's documents held together with sufficient binding.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large city in western Siberia on the Irtysh river.

clue.text: Vagrant outclasses no-hopers

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters of outclasses wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A tramp proves superior to the hopeless cases around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vagrant' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopeless causes or people with no chance of success are both described by this idiom.

clue.text: Plant spread easily in awkward position

indicators.note: in places the spreading word inside the awkward position

parts.note: to be in a corner is to be in an awkward position
liquids that spread easily flow

explanation.surface: A garden plant spreading readily even though it is planted in a tricky spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-flowered annual of grain fields, Centaurea cyanus, is a familiar garden plant.

clue.text: Material from journalist qualifying for booby prize?

parts.note: the booby prize goes to whoever does worst
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Fabric from a reporter who has earned the prize for last place.
explanation.walkthrough: A booby prize is a joke award for the worst performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine smooth woollen yarn and the cloth woven from it are this fabric.

clue.text: Crook's dabs on phone

indicators.note: heard on the phone, the word is judged only by its sound

parts.note: dabs of paint are small spots or flecks

explanation.surface: A criminal's fingerprints found on a telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dabs' is British slang for fingerprints, which suits the crook surface, but here it means small spots. 'on phone' says the word is heard rather than read.
explanation.definitionFit: To crook a finger or arm is to bend it, which is the meaning of the verb flex.

clue.text: Relatively buoyant container with loose lining

indicators.note: lining means the loose word sits inside the container, like a lining

parts.note: a jar is a container
to loose a knot is to untie it

explanation.surface: A description of a container that floats well with a loose lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' is a verb here, meaning to undo a knot, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunty means cheerful and lively in spirit, and the comparative form describes someone more buoyant.

clue.text: One's introduced fake coin in US (fifty imported)

indicators.note: imported means the fifty numeral is brought inside the rearranged letters
fake means the letters are counterfeited, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A counterfeit coin has entered the United States, with fifty brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'one that's introduced', a thing that has been added to a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added or brought into a group is an addition to it.

clue.text: Tourist's first hold-up, one believes

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the tourist word

parts.note: a heist is a robbery, a hold-up

explanation.surface: A tourist's first experience of a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: T from 'Tourist's first' goes before HEIST. The definition reads as 'one [who] believes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds faith in a god is a believer, which is what the term names.

clue.text: Runs through and stabs heartless Dickensian master

indicators.note: stabs means the word and is driven into the remaining letters
heartless means the central letter of the schoolmaster's name is removed

parts.note: Wackford Squeers is the cruel schoolmaster in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby

explanation.surface: A violent encounter: something runs through a cruel Dickens schoolmaster and stabs him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle E of SQUEERS, then 'stabs' pushes AND into the gap. 'Runs through' wants to mean pierces, but it is the money sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To run through money is to spend it recklessly and wastefully.

clue.text: Unbalanced shot bags ferret

indicators.note: bags means the shot letters enclose, pocket, the ferret word

parts.note: a shot is a photograph, a pic
a hob is a male ferret

explanation.surface: An unsteady shooter bags a ferret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unbalanced' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an irrational fear is in a mentally disturbed, unbalanced state about it.

clue.text: Frenchman behind bars, Republican held by priest in Dickens

indicators.note: in places the priest group inside the Dickens pen name

parts.note: Boz was the pen name Charles Dickens used early on

indicators.note: held by means the Republican letter sits inside the priest

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who trained Samuel

explanation.surface: A jailed Frenchman, with a Republican held by a priest in a Dickens story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind bars' suggests prison but means a composer, working behind musical bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a French Romantic composer, a man who wrote music in bars.

clue.text: Dispensed with for duration of broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so only the sound of the word matters

parts.note: throughout means for the whole duration of something

explanation.surface: Something done away with for the whole length of a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that the word for 'for duration of' is heard, not spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out something unwanted is to get rid of it, to do without it.

clue.text: Set upon course of action, ring up

parts.note: a way is a method, a course of action

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the ring word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to ring is to dial a phone number

explanation.surface: Deciding on a plan of action and then making a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay someone is to ambush or attack them, so the past tense means attacked.

clue.text: Mark close to bedside put off alarm

indicators.note: put off means that letter is removed from the alarm word

parts.note: to scare is to alarm

indicators.note: close to means the very end, the last letter of bedside

explanation.surface: A sleeper's bedside alarm clock is switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the end of 'bedside', is taken from SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: First couple of children always bringing happiness

indicators.note: first couple of means the opening two letters of the children word

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Children who always bring joy to a family.
explanation.walkthrough: E'er is the poetic contraction of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheer is a feeling of gladness and good spirits.

clue.text: Basic quality ultimately needed in lackey

indicators.note: needed in places that final letter inside the lackey word

parts.note: a lackey is a servile subordinate, an underling

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the quality word

explanation.surface: The fundamental quality that a good servant requires.
explanation.walkthrough: Y, the end of 'quality', goes inside UNDERLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lies beneath and supports everything else is fundamental or basic.

clue.text: Had enough for rail, nothing more

indicators.note: more means the nothing letter is added on after the rail word

parts.note: to rail against something is to rant
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Having had enough of complaining and not wanting any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' is the verb meaning complain angrily, not the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that ran to something was sufficient to cover it, stretching far enough.

clue.text: Drawing, not good, featuring current pioneering drug

indicators.note: featuring means the drawing word now includes the current symbol
not means the good letter is left out

parts.note: pencilling is drawing in pencil
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A sketch without merit showing a breakthrough medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' takes G from PENCILLING; 'featuring' puts I inside the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleming's antibiotic of 1928 was the first widely used antibiotic, a pioneering medicine.

clue.text: Verge to trim, about to be overlooked

indicators.note: to be overlooked means the about abbreviation is ignored and dropped

parts.note: to clip is to trim
C is circa, the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut the grass verge, though it is about to be forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verge' suggests a roadside grass strip, but it is the definition meaning edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lip is an edge or brim, the verge of a cup or a cliff.

clue.text: A qualified teacher, retired?

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching qualification

explanation.surface: Asking whether a qualified teacher has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests leaving a career, but here it means having gone to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired for the night is lying in bed.

clue.text: British artist leading religious school forward

indicators.note: leading puts the artist before the religious school

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A British painter at the head of a progressive religious movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a description of the school but is the definition, as in a forward manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward person is bold and shameless, lacking proper restraint.

clue.text: Most haughty French novelist from foreign parts

indicators.note: parts means the novelist's name is split open to admit the other word

parts.note: Marcel Proust was a French novelist
de is French for from

explanation.surface: An arrogant French writer from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word meaning arrogant or haughty.
